claims.text: A machine-learning interatomic potential trained on a sparse, strategically selected set of ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations can be used for free-energy evaluation near melting.
Targeted corrections can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling in the proposed ML free-energy workflow.
The proposed method can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed method can maintain accuracy comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
Active learning or reweighting can enforce physical constraints associated with vibrational and anharmonic effects.
The intended temperature domain extends from slightly below melting to approximately 1.1–1.2 times the melting temperature.
The initial pressure domain is ambient to moderately elevated pressure.
The ML surrogate can interpolate among configurations sampled by ab initio molecular dynamics and mediate free-energy integration across solid–liquid transitions.
Learning essential free-energy contributions from a limited number of ab initio simulations reduces the number of expensive electronic-structure evaluations required.
Reducing the number of expensive evaluations accelerates the workflow without sacrificing accuracy in free-energy differences.
The proposed method is expected to provide roughly an order-of-magnitude speedup over explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method is expected to provide roughly an order-of-magnitude speedup over TOR-TILD.
The method is expected to retain benchmark-comparable accuracy for free energies, melting temperatures, and vibrational contributions.
The hypothesis is expected to hold initially for elemental and binary systems near their melting points.
Extension to multicomponent high-entropy alloys requires additional validation because of greater phase complexity and interaction effects.
Preliminary evidence from simpler systems supports the proposed approach.
